verdict.headline: Hormuz draft unresolved as July payrolls loom — Brent $1.54 from the $85 trigger
verdict.label: Pre-NFP pause: Brent $83.46, 30Y sole breach at 5.20%, markets flat into 8:30 AM ET payrolls
verdict.rationale_short: The Bessent Hormuz framework remains fractured — Iran's restrictive draft awaits Khamenei approval, holding Brent at $83.46 and WTI at $78.05, each less than $1 or $2 from their respective regime triggers. July payrolls at 8:30 AM ET (consensus 83K, ADP 44K signal) is the session's resolving event: below 70K compresses September hike odds toward 35–40%; above 130K alongside Brent near $83 risks pushing the regime from 1-of-6 to 3-of-6. The 30Y at 5.20% remains the sole formal breach. SPCX Day 2 at ~$115 suggests the first 20% lockup tranche is absorbing rather than cascading. Level that changes the picture: SPX below 7,380 on a combined NFP-plus-oil shock.

watchlist_mentions.note: Day 2 after lockup at ~$115 — up ~6% from Aug 6 close of $108.27. Bloomberg confirmed the first 20% tranche (911.5M shares, ~$116B eligible) traded within a contained range on Day 1, with institutional buyers absorbing supply below $110 (intraday low $105.11). Day 2 stabilization signals absorption rather than delayed front-running. Next supply event is the 7% staggered tranche in 2-4 weeks. Q3 Starlink profitability (~October) is the only fundamental catalyst before the December 180-day terminal release. Above $120 on volume confirms the 20% tranche was structurally absorbed; below $105 on volume signals the next tranche is being front-run.

trade_setups.asset: NFP binary — July payrolls Friday 8:30 AM ET
trade_setups.thesis: The July NFP print (consensus 83K, prior 57K, ADP 44K) resolves the session's dominant uncertainty. September hike at 54% and 30Y at 5.20% give the print non-linear policy impact: below 70K confirms ADP's signal and should compress September odds toward 35–40%, creating a path for the 30Y to retrace toward 5.00%. Above 130K alongside Brent already near $83 risks pushing the regime from 1-of-6 to 3-of-6 in a single session — rate shock and oil shock arriving simultaneously.
trade_setups.entry: September hike probability on Kalshi within 10 minutes of the 8:30 AM ET release is the lead indicator. The 83–100K in-line range keeps September at 50–58% and the regime at 1-of-6, extending both variables unresolved into next week. The 7,380 SPX level is the structural backstop across all three scenarios.
trade_setups.invalidation: A print inside 83–100K with Brent below $80 confirms the base case without triggering either formal threshold — regime holds, no new information for directional resolution.
trade_setups.horizon: Binary event: 8:30 AM ET Friday. Market repricing: 1-2 sessions post-print.

trade_setups.thesis: Brent at $83.46 is $1.54 from the $85 formal breach threshold; WTI at $78.05 is $0.95 from the companion $79 gate. The Iranian draft plan — banning US/Israeli ships, imposing 20% cargo penalties — remains unapproved; Khamenei is the final gate. A combined breach of both oil triggers before the NFP print would add a second and third formal regime breach regardless of payrolls direction.
trade_setups.entry: Brent $85 and WTI $79 are the two thresholds. A signed Hormuz agreement or Iranian government retraction of the draft removes this setup and returns Brent toward the $78–80 range. Khamenei approval before 9:30 AM ET would activate the Brent breach ahead of the NFP data.
trade_setups.invalidation: Hormuz deal signed or draft retracted: Brent compresses below $80, oil gates clear, and the regime returns to 1-of-6 with 30Y as the sole breach.
trade_setups.horizon: Oil resolution: 24-48 hours pending Khamenei response. NFP overlay: 8:30 AM ET Friday.

trade_setups.asset: SaaS multiples — DDOG and Figma as leading indicators
trade_setups.thesis: Datadog fell 17% on a Q2 beat-and-raise (revenue $1.12B, +36%; FCF margin 29%→25%). Figma fell 16.5% on August 5 on the same setup. Both were at 25–30x NTM revenue before the print, both repriced to ~20–22x. Two consecutive SaaS names repricing on strong delivery from the same multiple band is the minimum evidence of a pattern. The next SaaS print (Snowflake or MongoDB, 2-4 weeks) tests whether it generalizes. If it does, PLTR (~98x forward sales) and NVDA at elevated multiples carry the comparative risk.
trade_setups.entry: DDOG's repriced level (~20–22x NTM) and the next SaaS print from a 25–30x NTM entry are the two data points. One observation is a data point; two or more establish a trend.
trade_setups.invalidation: A SaaS name delivering a beat-and-raise from 25–30x NTM and holding its multiple confirms DDOG and Figma are idiosyncratic — the reset does not generalize.
trade_setups.horizon: 2-4 weeks through remaining SaaS earnings season.

bear_case: NFP prints above 130K while Brent holds above $83 heading into the print: September hike probability breaks 70% (second breach), Brent clears $85 (third breach), and the 30Y extends above 5.20% — a 3-of-6 regime configuration in a single session that the 7,380 SPX floor would need to absorb. SPCX Day 2 stabilization at $115 is the bull case's strongest current signal; if Day 3 (Monday) sees a retest of $105 on volume, the absorption thesis fails and the next staggered 7% tranche becomes the front-run target, compressing SPCX toward $93–$100. The polysilicon Section 232 tariffs are a slow-burn supply-chain cost risk that may compound the Hormuz-NFP stack if August earnings calls reference it. If SPX reclaims 7,800 on a soft NFP print and Hormuz resolution, this read no longer holds.
